explanation: Inside the loop, `field` is correctly captured per-iteration via `const field = fields[i]`, which looks like it solves the classic loop-closure problem. But the `validate` function body doesn't use `field` at all — it reads `fields[i]` again. Because `i` is declared with `var`, it's function-scoped, not block-scoped, so by the time any stored validator is actually called (after the loop has finished), `i` has already advanced to `fields.length`. Every validator therefore reads `fields[fields.length]`, which is `undefined`, and `value.length <= undefined.maxLength` throws a TypeError regardless of which field's validator you invoke.
prompt: This factory is supposed to build one independent validator per field. What's the bug?
choices: `validate` reads `fields[i]` instead of the locally captured `field`, and since `i` is declared with `var` it has already advanced to `fields.length` by the time any validator is called, so every validator reads `undefined`
`field` should be declared with `let` instead of `const` so it can be reassigned on each iteration
`validators[field.name]` silently overwrites earlier entries because object keys must be unique strings
The loop condition should use `i <= fields.length` to include the last field
This code is correct — `const field = fields[i]` already re-binds a fresh variable every iteration, so the closures are safely isolated
